If anything is missing, go back and fix it before you save. - [ ] The **title** describes what the plot shows, in plain language, and doesn't claim that one thing causes another. - [ ] The **x-axis and y-axis labels** are plain language (no variable names like `food_insecure` or question codes like `Q27`). - [ ] The y-axis label says these are **percents** (e.g., "Percent of respondents"). - [ ] Findings 2 and 3: the **legend** has a plain-language title. - [ ] The **categories** are in a meaningful order (low to high, or worst to best), not alphabetical. - [ ] There's **no "NA" bar** or "NA" segment, and no "Refused" or "Don't know" category. - [ ] The **percent labels** are readable and don't overlap. - [ ] Someone who has never seen your data could understand the plot **without reading your code**. ::: 1. **Make a `plots` folder.** [`ggsave()`](https://nwakim.github.io/PUBH_523_26F/lessons/32_Data_viz_Design_choices/Data_viz_Design_choices.html#/saving-plots) can't create a folder for you: if the folder doesn't exist, you'll get an error like `Cannot find directory`. In RStudio's **Files** pane, go to your class folder (the one with your `.Rproj` file), click **New Folder**, and name it `plots`. 2. **Save each plot with `ggsave()`** (Lesson 32). Use [`here()`](https://nwakim.github.io/PUBH_523_26F/lessons/12_Rproj_wds/Rproj_wds.html#/the-here-package) to point to your `plots` folder, give each file a descriptive name, and tell `ggsave()` which plot to save: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggsave( filename = here("plots", "finding1_ease_free_food.png"), plot = finding1_plot, width = 6, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white" ) ``` ::: - `bg = "white"` gives the image a white background. Without it, [`theme_minimal()`](https://nwakim.github.io/PUBH_523_26F/lessons/32_Data_viz_Design_choices/Data_viz_Design_choices.html#/complete-themes) plots are saved with a see-through background, and the text can disappear on a dark screen or slide. - Save at `dpi = 300` or higher so your plot looks crisp on a printed page. - Use a descriptive file name for each plot (e.g., `finding1_...`, `finding2_...`) so they're easy to find later. - Change `width` and `height` if your labels look crowded.
